description:
## Goal

Make product work measurable across both a cold root request and later requests in the same long-lived compiler, so implementation tickets optimize proven producer evaluations rather than logs that blur population, displacement, recursive publication, and retained reuse.

The causal telemetry prerequisite has landed. fz-tfn.25 stabilizes recursive-search counts and traversal work on the current graph before this ticket. Exact recursive publication membership remains explicitly owned by fz-tfn.2 after fz-kdt.4 removes the schedule-dependent eager RuntimeDemand cone.

## Required measurements

For each target fixture, record one causal report covering:

1. cold root request;
2. unchanged second request in the same Compiler2;
3. redefinition of an unreachable function followed by the same root request;
4. redefinition of one reached leaf followed by the same root request;
5. redefinition that retracts one old callee and introduces another.

Count by exact ProductKey and request: first production, retained cache hit, displacement, reproduction, equal reproduction, distinct demanded keys, producer evaluations, exact causing fact/product movement, recursive search counts/work, scheduler evaluations/work-start reason, and final reachable executable/wrapper population.

## Output contract

- Product request, producer evaluation, settlement, cache hit, displacement, and recursive-peer publication are distinct.
- Identity and causality are raw structured values; formatted Debug strings are never authority.
- Requests in one Compiler2 cannot be conflated.
- Every non-initial evaluation names exact dependency movement or is reported as unexplained.
- Search counts and traversal work are reproducible through fz-tfn.25.
- Exact recursive publication membership is reported faithfully but may differ on the temporary eager-cone graph; the report names that single explicit dimension, which fz-tfn.2 removes after fz-kdt.4. The already-proven CallableConstruction cache-hit redistribution remains separately named.
- The harness observes production APIs, remains as the work-count regression signal, and introduces no stopwatch threshold or shadow cache.

## Acceptance

- Baseline reports for 00420_enum_take_drop_split, enum_predicate_search, and fz_f98_range_map_converges are reproducible.
- Cold population, within-request churn, and cross-request recomputation are distinct dimensions.
- Unchanged and irrelevant-edit cases expose current fresh-session repopulation directly.
- Recursive search work is attributable to changed dependency edges versus discovery and is stable across processes.
- Repeated processes produce identical causal work multisets except only the two explicit, already-owned temporary dimensions above.
- Documentation explains how to reproduce/read the report and points exact recursive membership to fz-tfn.2.

This ticket measures and installs the permanent signal. It does not optimize the compiler.

fz-tfn.25 found one pre-existing enum_predicate_search causal gap on c521: DeriveExecutableFacts for Enum.any?/2#lambda@4599-4650/2 over main lambda@3054-3113 re-evaluates after settled ActivationAnalyzed/CallSiteSummary movement, changes nothing, then blocks on ActivationAnalyzed. The triggering AnalyzeActivation completion carries the target poststates only in movements, not changed before/after, so replay classifies no cause. Exact command: target/debug/fz2 --log-telemetry TRACE interp fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz. The current fz-kdt.46 exact-wait candidate eliminates this gap; its three-target reads+blocked causal regression is green. Recheck and remove any temporary exception when fz-kdt.46 is integrated before closing kdt.5.

title: Establish cold and incremental product-work causality before optimization
